title: Sprint 12 intake triage — surge cut plan & wireframe notes
content:
Context / goal:
- Sprint 12 is constrained: 2 devs full-time equivalent for console infra, 1 UX designer, 0.4 PM. Goal is a minimal, testable cut that improves intake signal routing so SLOs are easier to enforce and triage surfaces for on-call.
- This doc captures intake triage heuristics, proposed cutlist, rough wireframe sketches, acceptance criteria, and owner assignments for the surge sprint.

Guiding principles for cuts (decision heuristics):
1) Safety-first: any change that could fail open or hide errors -> defer.
2) Observability payoff: prefer items that give high-signal telemetry per engineering effort (example: token-level latency breakdown card).
3) Quick wins: <3 dev-days and measurable uplift get priority.
4) Dependency minimization: favor items that don't add infra dependencies (no new backend services unless necessary).
5) UX clarity > visual polish for this sprint: ship plain but unambiguous states.

Capacity assumptions:
- Dev capacity: ~80 dev-hours per week across two engineers (x2 weeks) = 320 dev-hours. Accounting for meetings and bug-fixes, target ~240h usable.
- Designer: 2 days of wireframe + handoff.
- QA: 16 hours.

Prioritized cutlist (proposed order, with rough estimates):
A. Intake routing: quick triage rules editor (toggle-based) — 5d, owner: Marco
   - Deliverable: toggle UI to enable/disable rules, simple validation, save to existing feature-flag store.
   - Rationale: enables immediate manual mitigation without deploy.
   - Acceptance: toggles persist, toggles reflected in routing (smoke-test), unit tests + e2e toggle smoke.

B. Triage inbox view: add "stale" and "priority" filters + compact row view — 4d, owner: Riley
   - Deliverable: new filters + compact rows, counts in header.
   - Rationale: reduces scrolling and surfaces hot issues to on-call.
   - Acceptance: filter combinations work, counts match API, accessible keyboard nav.

C. Telemetry card: per-route median and p95 latency microcard — 3d, owner: Naomi
   - Deliverable: collapsed card with sparkline + p95 badge.
   - Rationale: high signal, low UI surface.
   - Acceptance: data matches observability traces within 5%, toggles to change time window.

D. Wireframe: inline rule-preview modal (static mock) — 1d design, 1d dev hookup, owner: Riley
   - Deliverable: modal showing current triage logic in plain language.
   - Rationale: reduces config errors by clarifying outcome.

E. Rollout safety: add "dry-run" flag to rules editor (no traffic effect) — 2d, owner: Marco
   - Deliverable: dry-run persists but doesn't change routing; logs show matched examples.

Lower-priority / defer list:
- Full visual rule builder (drag-drop) -> defer (big infra + UX).
- Auto-suggest rules from traffic patterns -> defer to Optimize roadmap.
- Cross-team rollout orchestration UI -> defer (requires backend changes).

Wireframe notes (designer pointers and ASCII sketches):
- Main triage header: compact counts (open / priority / stale) at top-left. Filters inline.
- Row layout: 3-line compact: [route name] — [severity badge] \u2022 [last seen] on first line; second line shows small summary of matched rule; third line shows last 3 events (tokens, latency).
- Rule editor modal sketch (very rough):
  +-------------------------------+
  | Rule name [_____]  [Active: o] |
  | Conditions:                     |
  |  [when latency >] [500ms] [AND] |
  | Actions: [mark priority] [dry-run o] |
  +-------------------------------+
- Rule-preview modal should show 3 example matching requests (anonymized) and why they matched. Keep examples small (path, p95, sample tokens).

Acceptance criteria (sprint-ready):
- All A/B items shipped behind feature flag.
- Smoke test script in repo (tests/smoke/intake-triage.md) updated and passing in CI.
- UX: keyboard navigable lists, 90% of story points have design reviewed annotations.
- Observability: new telemetry card must match Prometheus/Trace data with a documented query in linked PR.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: toggles not honored by runtime due to caching.
  Mitigation: add immediate publish endpoint that flushes routing cache; test in staging.
- Risk: UI change causes support confusion.
  Mitigation: add short tooltip copy + Slack announcement draft (see linked Slack thread).

Open questions (decisions needed during grooming):
1) Persist rules in feature-flag store vs. a new small table? (Pref: feature flags for speed; ops concern about auditability.)
2) Should dry-run logs be retained for more than 7 days? Cost/retention trade-off.
3) What is the definition of "stale" for triage? 72 hours or 7 days? Proposal: start with 72h for sprint, iterate.

Next steps / owner actions before sprint kickoff:
- Marco: prototype toggles (skeleton) and post a demo in #console-product by EOD Fri.
- Riley: deliver wireframes and row comp spec by Wed.
- Naomi (PM): update tickets with acceptance criteria, link smoke test doc, create QA checklist.
- All: quick run of staging smoke test on Thu alongside SRE.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally thin: focus on safety and observability. If you think an item is mis-prioritized, add a comment with impact estimate.
- If you need sample API shapes or queries, see linked PR and Confluence page in linked_artifacts.

Quick links used during grooming:
- Slack thread: #console-triage (see message timestamp 2024-09-11 10:32)
- Related tickets: RINF-2123 (intake routing toggles), RINF-2118 (triage inbox filters)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/899 (telemetry-card prototype)

Changelog for this doc:
- 2024-09-12 Naomi: initial draft and cutlist.
- 2024-09-15 Marco: added dry-run approach and cache flush mitigation.
- 2024-09-18 Riley: updated wireframe ASCII and acceptance criteria after design review.

Random notes / scratchpad (keep, may be cleaned later):
- Consider a single-click "escalate" action that opens a prepopulated incident link. Low-effort if we reuse existing template.
- Add small inline help: why priority vs severity (one-liner).
- If time, add a simple onboarding tooltip for on-call to explain the new triage states.

-- end of doc --
